column1: # Kids stand-in photographs — TEST DATA

# product borrows the nearest delivered adult photograph so the Kids section can be seen and
# tested. THE REAL PHOTOGRAPHS ARE STILL OUTSTANDING; nothing here is finished work.
# This file is the single authoritative list. `tools/kids-stand-in-photos.ps1` reads it
# `KidsStandInMappingTests` holds every slug in it against the real catalogue
# a product that does not exist fails the build rather than the import.
# Quality is an honest grade of the match
column2: not a label on the picture:

column1: #   exact  the same garment in the same material
#   good   the same garment type; one property (fabric
#   fair   the same construction or the same cloth
#   poor   only one property carries over; a viewer will see the wrong garment
#   none   nothing in the delivery is close — recorded so nobody mistakes it for a match

KidsSlug
girls-cotton-sundress
column6: The nearest one-piece light dress in the delivery: unstructured, gathered and summer-weight, and the tiering reads as a sundress silhouette. It is an adult woman in the frame, so the scale and the body are wrong.

column1: girls-printed-tee
column6: The only printed cotton jersey tee delivered, and the print is the defining feature of the kids product. Boxy where the kids tee is a regular fit.

column1: girls-jersey-leggings
column6: Exactly the same garment — full-length leggings with a covered waistband. The knit is a performance seamless rather than cotton jersey, so the surface is wrong and the shape is right.

column1: boys-checked-shirt
column6: Same construction: a woven cotton shirt with a button-down collar, which is the detail the kids product leads on. Nothing checked was delivered, so the pattern is wrong and only the pattern.

column1: boys-cotton-tee-two-pack
column6: A plain taped-shoulder crew-neck tee in pure cotton — the garment and the fabric both match. One tee is in frame where the product is a two-pack, so the count is wrong.

column1: boys-pull-on-shorts
column6: Pull-on shorts cut above the knee with an elastic back and a flat drawcord, which is the closure the kids product is named for. Linen rather than a cotton blend. Chino Shorts were rejected: a flat front with a zip is the wrong closure, which is the one thing a shopper is looking at here.

column1: baby-ribbed-bodysuit-set
column6: The only ribbed cotton jersey in the delivery, and the rib is the one property that carries over. A bodysuit is not a tee and no babywear at all was delivered, so a viewer sees an adult top, not a bodysuit set.

column1: baby-muslin-bib-set
column6: Nothing in the delivery is close: there is no bib, no muslin and no flat cloth accessory. The tote is chosen only because it is a plain woven-cotton accessory photographed as an object rather than a garment on an adult body — on a baby product that is the less misleading of the two available errors. It is a bag; treat this row as a gap, not a match.

column1: kids-canvas-sneakers
column6: The same shoe in the same materials: a cotton canvas upper with a reinforced toe on a vulcanised rubber sole, low profile. Only the closure differs (laces, where the kids shoe is hook-and-loop).

column1: girls-denim-pinafore
column6: Washed denim cut as a short A-line skirt, and denim is what a pinafore is bought for. The bib and the adjustable straps — the half that makes it a pinafore — are not in the picture. Belted Shirt Dress was rejected: the dress shape is closer, the cloth is not, and denim is the stronger cue.
